items.q: A factory has 23 employees, each paid £60 a day. It produces 200 units a day and sells each for £15. What are employee costs as a percentage of turnover?
items.why: Each day: employee costs = 23 × £60 = £1,380; turnover = 200 × £15 = £3,000. Employee costs as % of turnover = £1,380 ÷ £3,000 × 100 = 46%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A factory can produce 3,000 units a month. It produced 1,850 units last month. What is its capacity utilisation?
items.why: Capacity utilisation = actual output ÷ maximum possible output × 100 = 1,850 ÷ 3,000 × 100 = 61.7%.
items.label: New question

items.q: Biggs Ltd, 2023 (£000): revenue 47,569; gross profit 22,289; operating profit 4,650; payables 5,056. Calculate its payables days.
items.why: Cost of sales = revenue – gross profit = 47,569 – 22,289 = 25,280. Payables days = 5,056 ÷ 25,280 × 365 = 73 days. Using revenue instead of cost of sales gives 38.8 days.
items.label: Paper 2 June 2024 Q01.1

items.q: Company X has 40% market share. Market size declines by 20%. No other changes. Company X's market share now is:
items.why: If original market = 100, X's sales = 40. Market falls 20% to 80. X's sales unchanged at 40. New share = 40/80 x 100 = 50%. 'No other changes' means X's sales stay at 40. Only the overall market shrank.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A business has an opening cash balance of £30,000 for March. Cash inflows in March are £65,000 and cash outflows are £70,000. What is the closing balance?
items.why: Net cash flow = inflows – outflows = £65,000 – £70,000 = –£5,000. Closing balance = opening balance + net cash flow = £30,000 – £5,000 = £25,000.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business budgeted income of £85m and expenditure of £73m. Actual income was 5% above budget and actual expenditure was 5% above budget. What is the profit variance?
items.why: Budgeted profit = £85m – £73m = £12m. Actual income = £89.25m, actual expenditure = £76.65m, so actual profit = £12.60m. Variance = £12.60m – £12m = £0.60m favourable (profit is higher than budgeted).
items.label: New question

items.q: In 2016: 12 employees, 60 units output, 75% capacity utilisation. In 2017: 100% capacity utilisation, same workforce. Labour productivity per employee in 2017?
items.why: First find capacity: if 60 units = 75% of capacity, then capacity = 60/0.75 = 80 units. At 100% utilisation, output = 80 units. LP = 80/12 = 6.67 units per employee. You must first calculate capacity from the 2016 data before calculating 2017 productivity. Capacity = actual output / utilisation rate.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Use the break-even chart. What is the break-even output?
items.why: Break-even is where the total revenue and total costs lines cross, at 400 units. You can check: fixed costs £2,000 ÷ contribution per unit of £5 = 400 units.
items.label: New question

items.q: A product has a price elasticity of demand of -2. The price rises by 5%. What happens to quantity demanded and sales revenue?
items.why: % change in quantity = PED × % change in price = -2 × +5% = -10%. Demand is elastic, so revenue moves the opposite way to price: it falls.
items.label: New question

items.q: Righton plc, 2024 (£m): non-current assets 335; inventories 80; receivables 35; cash 40; payables 70; net current assets 85; non-current liabilities 230; total equity 190. Calculate its current ratio.
items.why: Current assets = 80 + 35 + 40 = £155m. Current liabilities = payables £70m. Current ratio = 155 ÷ 70 = 2.21:1.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2025 Q16
